A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same rank/Chain-of-Thought research, with readable definitions, equations, constructions, and proofs. All 20 pages of v1 and 27 pages of v2 support comparison. Neither contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports mathematical characterizations and proofs of decoder-depth bounds, without original experiments, simulations, user studies, or empirical data analyses.

after.justification: v2 adds theoretical learning algorithms and complexity proofs. Its labeled samples and sample matrices are mathematical constructions, not empirical study outcomes.

M1.justification: The decoder architecture and existing constructions remain unchanged, but Section 6.1 introduces a recursive consistency algorithm for fixed-rank functions over arbitrary fixed finite alphabets. It identifies lower-rank-consistent subsamples, recursively processes the remaining samples, and assembles a decision tree. v1 contains no corresponding learning procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or tasks for empirical training or evaluation. The new PAC-consistency problems are studied mathematically.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates competing methods. The added comparison with hardness results for 2-term DNFs concerns theoretical positioning, not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Neither version contains experimental evaluation protocols. Section 6's sample-access assumptions and accuracy parameters define a theoretical learning model.

E4.justification: Neither version reports empirical ablations, robustness tests, or supplementary experimental analyses. The new examples and gadgets support proofs.

E5.justification: Neither reports repeated experimental runs or statistical uncertainty estimates. v2's PAC confidence parameter is a formal guarantee, not uncertainty reporting from experiments.

E6.justification: Neither version reports measured performance, empirical rankings, or observed qualitative outcomes. The added learnability and hardness results are mathematical contributions assessed under T1.

T1.justification: New Section 6 formalizes PAC learning and consistency, proves polynomial-time consistency for fixed single-head rank over finite alphabets (Theorem 4), and proves NP-completeness for Boolean two-head rank at most one (Theorem 5). Lemmas 3–6 provide the algorithmic argument and reduction machinery. The original rank/decoder equivalences and CoT bounds are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add PAC learnability as a main contribution: proper learning for bounded single-head rank, improper learning for bounded multi-head rank, and conditional hardness of proper learning already for two-head rank one. Multi-head rank itself was already introduced in v1.

C2.justification: Section 6 explains why efficient learning through a larger single-head hypothesis class yields only improper learning of the multi-head class. New Section 7 qualifies comparisons with multilayer soft-attention results by explaining their different input encoding, with an entire function supplied in one token.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies implementation, hardware, training, or code/data-access information. The new constructive algorithm is described mathematically rather than accompanied by implementation details.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Valiant, Kearns and Vazirani, Pitt and Valiant, Schaefer, and Chen et al. It positions its learning-hardness theorem as incomparable with 2-term-DNF hardness and distinguishes Chen et al.'s composition setting. The existing Transformer-expressivity positioning remains largely intact.

P1.justification: The earlier sections remain largely intact. v2 makes local language and notation edits, clarifies the Section 5.2 proof, moves Proposition 6's discussion after that proof, adopts author–year citations, and extends the abstract and roadmap for Sections 6–7.

P2.justification: v2 adds an unnumbered paired tabular display of positive and negative gadget samples in Section 6.2, page 23. Equation displays and bibliography formatting also change, while the overall single-column presentation is retained.

improvement.justification: v1 motivates rank through PAC learning but does not examine learnability of its multi-head generalization. Section 6 of v2 addresses that substantive question with a constructive algorithm and detailed hardness reductions, distinguishing efficient improper learning from conditional proper-learning hardness. This substantially deepens the computational implications of the characterization while preserving the original CoT results.
